run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:55:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert context states RequestErrorRate (severity warning) for service_name=frontend-proxy in namespace otel-demo since 2026-11-16T13:55:08Z with current value 0.02222222222222222. In this target, frontend-proxy exposes only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so its error-rate signal is the span-call counter. That counter's frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR series rose from 514 at 13:43:08 to 543 at 13:47:08 and 583 at 13:48:08 (+69), and the same +69 appears in checkout's CLIENT span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (ERROR), checkout's SERVER span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (ERROR) and frontend's SERVER span POST /api/checkout (ERROR); frontend-proxy access logs show POST /api/checkout returning HTTP 500 via_upstream in that interval. The failure point is the payment call: the payment Deployment was restarted at 13:45:30 (template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:45:30Z), its only pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 was deleted at 13:45:33, the replacement payment-54499f9786-4r25d started its container at 13:45:33 but its log shows 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 13:46:48.571, and the payment Deployment has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, so the rollout removed the old backend before the new one could serve. The payment charge span counter froze at 1100 across 13:47:00-13:48:00 and resumed at 1142 at 13:49:00. 69 error spans out of roughly 3100 frontend-proxy spans is a ratio of about 1/45 = 0.0222, matching the alert's current value. A separate, much smaller error source exists: intermittent 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on the frontend upstream (about 1 per 1-2 minutes) that does not explain a 2.22% ratio. The exact alert rule is not visible in this Prometheus, so the rule arithmetic is stated as a hypothesis.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR: the raw counter is 505 at the earliest returned sample 13:24:08, 514 at 13:43:08, 543 at 13:47:08, 583 at 13:48:08, and 593 at 14:00:08, while the STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress counter grows by roughly 600-700 per minute through the window; frontend-proxy's 'router frontend egress' ERROR series moves in lockstep with ingress.

A single +69 error burst is visible in three independent services over 13:46-13:48: frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 514 -> 543 -> 583 (+69); checkout's CLIENT span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 28 at 13:47:00 to 69 at 13:48:00 and stayed 69; frontend's SERVER span POST /api/checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR went 87 -> 115 at 13:46:30 (+28) -> 156 at 13:47:30 (+41) and stayed 156 through 14:05:00. (increase() values in other queries over-count these increments; the raw counters above are authoritative. Span counts are not unique request counts.)

frontend-proxy access logs show HTTP 500 responses on the checkout route in that interval, for example 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' at 13:46:50.603, 13:46:55.935, 13:46:56.035, 13:47:00.001, 13:47:04.402 and onward through 13:47:17.874 (25 newest of 71 matching 5xx lines in 13:44:00-13:52:00), i.e. the frontend answered with an application error (via_upstream), not a connection failure.

The failing step is the payment call: checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span is SPAN_KIND_CLIENT and carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR (69 increments), checkout's oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder is SPAN_KIND_SERVER with the same error series, while payment's own spans (charge SPAN_KIND_INTERNAL, grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge) show STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series at all.

Payment stopped serving during the rollout: payment's charge span counter is 1094 at 13:46:00, frozen at 1100 for both 13:47:00 and 13:48:00, then 1142 at 13:49:00, and the replacement pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 13:46:48.571 with its first 'Charge request received.' at 13:47:21.971, even though its container started at 13:45:33.

The payment Deployment in namespace otel-demo was restarted at 13:45:30: .spec.template.metadata.annotations[kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt] = 2026-11-16T13:45:30Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%, and readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe are all null for container 'payment'. ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 was created 13:45:30 with 1 replica and payment-55766d76b9 (created 13:13:18) was scaled to 0.

The rollout events in otel-demo are exactly: Deployment/payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1' at 13:45:30, ReplicaSet/payment-54499f9786 'Created pod: payment-54499f9786-4r25d' at 13:45:30, pod Scheduled 13:45:30, container Created/Started 13:45:32/13:45:33, Deployment/payment 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 13:45:33 and ReplicaSet/payment-55766d76b9 'Deleted pod: payment-55766d76b9-846r8' (with 'Stopping container payment') at 13:45:33 - i.e. the old pod was removed ~75s before the new process listened.

Among all 21 Deployments in otel-demo, only payment has restartedAt inside the incident period (2026-11-16T13:45:30Z); flagd has restartedAt 2026-11-16T13:15:12Z and the other 19 are null. No Deployment other than otel-collector has a readinessProbe.

A separate, low-rate error source exists on the same proxy: frontend-proxy logs show 'GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with upstream cluster 'frontend' at 13:47:42.903, 13:50:58.215, 13:53:35.051, 13:53:50.791, 13:54:23.826, 13:54:37.351, 13:57:21.816 and 13:58:24.351, interspersed with normal 200 via_upstream responses. The matching ingress ERROR counter increased only about +10 between 13:48:08 and 14:00:08.

Error spans appear before and independent of the payment restart: frontend's POST /api/checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter already stood at 87 at 13:35:00 (first sample of that series), and frontend-proxy's ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter was already 505 at its first sample 13:24:08, rising only to 514 by 13:43:08. All pods in otel-demo report start times between 13:13:17 and 13:15:12 (payment 13:13:18, checkout 13:15:05, frontend 13:13:21, frontend-proxy 13:13:22, flagd 13:15:12).

In the 13:43:00-13:53:00 window the only services with STATUS_CODE_ERROR series were frontend-proxy ('router frontend egress' 72.6, 'ingress' 74.7), frontend ('grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout' about 72.6 each), checkout ('oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' about 43.2), plus single small series in ad, recommendation and fraud-detection on 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (1.05 each); no other service shows errors. (These are increase() values and are not unique request counts.)

frontend-proxy's own pod and the frontend pod are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt container started 13:13:21, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks started 13:13:22), the Services 'frontend' and 'frontend-proxy' each have exactly one ready address, and the checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp is Ready with restartCount 0 (started 13:15:05). Checkout logs after the burst at 13:53 show repeated successful 'payment went through', 'order placed' and 'order confirmation email sent' sequences.

The only metric families returned for service_name="frontend-proxy" are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so the RequestErrorRate signal available for frontend-proxy is the span-call counter split by status_code.

A pod-level outage of the alerting service is not the explanation: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks is Ready, has restartCount 0 since 13:13:22, has no previous container instance, and its STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress counter kept growing throughout (5847 at 13:24:08 to 31725 by 14:01:08), so the proxy itself kept serving.

The ongoing 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} events cannot explain the alert value: only 8 such lines appear between 13:47:42 and 13:58:24 and the ingress ERROR counter grew by about 10 over 13:48:08-14:00:08 (roughly 0.03% of ~600-700 spans/minute), far below a 2.22% ratio; their affected requests also produce no frontend error span, only the proxy's egress error.

Rejected: the checkout service itself broke. checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp is Ready with restartCount 0 (started 13:15:05), its only error spans are the CLIENT oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and the enclosing oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, and its logs at 13:53 show orders completing with 'payment went through'.

Rejected: the frontend pod was down or crashing. frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt is Ready with restartCount 0 since 13:13:21 and one Service endpoint, and the proxy logged HTTP 500 via_upstream for POST /api/checkout (an application response that reached the frontend) while other routes on the same pod returned 200 at the same time.

Rejected as this cause: the flagd restart (restartedAt 2026-11-16T13:15:12Z) being considered as the trigger of the frontend-proxy error burst. It precedes the alert by about 40 minutes, and the only error series touching flagd are single 1.05-increase series on 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' in ad, recommendation and fraud-detection, with no tie to the checkout error path.

The alert's value 0.02222222222222222 is best explained by the burst: 69 frontend-proxy ingress error spans out of roughly 3100 spans in a short (about 5 minute) evaluation window, i.e. 69/3105 = 1/45 = 0.0222, with the 13:55:08 start reflecting the alert's pending/for period after the 13:46-13:48 increments. This is a hypothesis because the RequestErrorRate rule itself returned no data in this Prometheus and its exact expression, window and threshold are unknown.

Mechanism: because the payment Deployment defines no readinessProbe, the replacement pod was considered Ready as soon as its container started at 13:45:33, so the ReplicaSet scaled the only serving pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 to 0 at 13:45:33 while the new process only began listening at 13:46:48; during that gap checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls failed (69 error spans), the failure propagated to oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, then to frontend POST /api/checkout HTTP 500, and surfaced at frontend-proxy as ingress error spans.

The recurring 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on the 'frontend' upstream looks like an Envoy/upstream keep-alive connection-termination race rather than a frontend failure: the resets are intermittent across GET /api/products, /api/cart and /api/data, the frontend pod is Ready with 0 restarts, and the sampled error traces show the proxy egress span with http.status_code 0 and no corresponding frontend span. This remains unverified from the frontend side.

A second candidate contributor to a non-zero error ratio is the namespace-wide pod start between 13:13:17 and 13:15:12, before the first span-metric sample: 505 frontend-proxy ingress error spans already existed at 13:24:08 and 87 frontend POST /api/checkout error spans already existed at 13:35:00 with no rollout in between. Whether these contribute to the reported value depends on the unknown alert window and remains unresolved.

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) to the payment Deployment's container so a rolling update cannot remove the only payment pod before the gRPC server listens; this is the specific configuration gap that turned the 13:45:30 restart into a ~75s backend gap.

Treat the 2026-11-16T13:45:30Z payment rollout as a restart-induced availability gap: identify who or what applied the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:45:30Z annotation (change history is not available in this Run), and consider running payment with more than one replica plus a PodDisruptionBudget so a restart cannot empty the Service.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule for frontend-proxy (threshold, window and for-duration). A 69-error burst confined to a ~75s dependency outage produces a 2.22% ratio once diluted over only ~3100 spans; a rule using a longer window plus a minimum absolute error count, or excluding client-side/dependency-induced errors, would reduce warning noise. Also consider a short retry/backoff for UNAVAILABLE on checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client.

Investigate the intermittent 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} between frontend-proxy and the frontend upstream: align Envoy upstream idle/keep-alive timeouts with the frontend HTTP server settings and evaluate an upstream retry policy, since these resets are the only error source still present after 13:48.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule itself is not visible: list_prometheus_rules returned no data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the exact expression, evaluation window, threshold and for-duration cannot be verified; the 69/~3105 = 0.0222 arithmetic is an inference.

Jaeger trace data ends around 13:41 and returned no traces for 13:44-13:56 (empty results for frontend-proxy, checkout and POST /api/checkout error searches), so the 13:46-13:48 burst could not be inspected span by span and the sampled traces cover only 13:20-13:38.
Fetching frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt logs returned zero lines for 13:40-14:11, so the frontend's application-side error text for the POST /api/checkout 500 responses is unknown.
checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp logs contained no lines matching error/fail/exception/refus/unavailable/charge keywords in 13:40-14:05, so the exact gRPC status returned by the payment call is unknown.

kube-state-metrics series kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_pod_container_info returned no data for the payment Deployment/pods, so the readiness timeline cannot be confirmed from metrics and the old vs new payment image digests cannot be compared (only the identical 2.1.3-payment image tag in the current spec is known).
Kubernetes events for otel-demo cover only 13:45:30-13:45:33, so nothing is known about events around the namespace-wide pod start at 13:13-13:15 or about any earlier changes.
The change_history integration is not available, so who or what applied the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:45:30Z change to the payment Deployment could not be determined.

frontend-proxy span-metric series begin only at 13:24:08, so error increments before that time (including the 505 errors already present at the first sample) are unknown and the 13:13-13:15 startup transient could not be quantified.

Whether the alert's ratio is computed over a short (~5m) or long/cumulative window cannot be checked, so the relative contribution of the 13:46-13:48 burst versus the earlier 13:13-13:24 accumulation remains unresolved.

No application-level metric distinguishes HTTP 500 from 503 on the frontend-proxy span series (http status is a span tag, not a metric label), so per-status error counts in the burst are known only from the sampled access logs.
next_steps: Ask the platform owner to publish or export the RequestErrorRate alert rule (expression, window, threshold, for-duration) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus instance that fired it, to confirm the 5-minute ratio interpretation.
Audit the source of kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:45:30Z on Deployment payment (CI/CD or operator) and add a readinessProbe before any further restart.

If deeper confirmation is needed, reproduce with a payment rollout in a test namespace and verify that checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge errors occur exactly while the old pod is deleted and the new pod has not yet logged its gRPC server start.

Inspect frontend and checkout container stdout/stderr outside this Run's retention limits (the frontend stream returned no lines), if longer log retention exists, to capture the exact error message behind the HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
